holidays.name: National Peanut Butter and Jelly Day
holidays.description: A salute to the sweet-meets-salty sandwich that has rescued lunchboxes for generations. Today is the day to slather, stack, squish and snack. Crusts are optional, and so is the debate over which goes on first.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food holiday, and the sandwich behind it has a long history. One of the earliest known mentions of pairing peanut butter with jelly on bread appeared in 1901. Another popular story credits American soldiers in World War II, who combined their peanut butter and jelly rations into a sandwich.
holidays.funFact: The average American is said to eat well over a thousand PB&Js by high school graduation. Some estimates run past 1,500.

holidays.name: National Ride Your Horse to a Bar Day
holidays.description: A cowboy-flavored invitation to trade your car keys for a set of reins and trot up to your favorite watering hole. Hitching posts are encouraged, and so is a designated sober rider, or at least a very sensible horse. Cowboy hats are always welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance of unclear origin. It draws on the Wild West image of tying up outside the saloon. Western communities have embraced it, and some viewers have taken it literally and ridden to a bar.
holidays.funFact: Local news stations have covered people who took the holiday literally and rode their horses to the pub.
